A used couch can be a genuine score — [most sell for a fraction of retail](/blog/home-cleaning/how-much-is-a-used-couch-worth/) — but it arrives carrying the previous owner's entire history: skin cells, dander, odors, and occasionally passengers. The cleaning sequence below handles everything that's handleable. Just as important: the inspection that tells you whether to bring it inside at all.

## Before It Crosses Your Threshold: The Inspection

Do this at pickup, in daylight, before money changes hands if possible:

- **Check for bed bugs.** Pull back cushions and inspect seams, zippers, and frame crevices for dark spotting (droppings), shed skins, or the bugs themselves — about apple-seed sized. **This is the one absolute deal-breaker.** No cleaning method below reliably clears an infestation, and bringing one home can cost thousands.
- **Smell it honestly.** Smoke and pet odor live in foam, not fabric — if you can smell it outdoors, you'll smell it more in your living room.
- **Press for moisture and check the underside** for water stains or mildew spotting — [mold inside a couch isn't cleanable](/blog/home-cleaning/moldy-couch-removal-tips-when-to-replace/).
- **Check the care tag code** — W or W/S means water-based cleaning is safe; S or X limits everything below to vacuuming and professional solvent cleaning.

## The Sanitizing Sequence

**1. Quarantine and vacuum first.** Garage or covered porch if you can. HEPA-vacuum every surface slowly — seams, crevices, underside, both faces of every cushion. This removes the loose layer so later steps work on what's bonded.

**2. Hot-wash everything removable.** Covers and cushion cases at 130°F+, dried fully on high. This alone resolves most of what a used couch carries, which is why removable covers are the best feature a secondhand sofa can have.

**3. Steam clean the body** (W/W-S fabrics only). Rent a steam cleaner, work in overlapping passes, and keep the fabric damp — not soaked. Heat is doing the sanitizing here.

**4. Treat odors enzymatically.** For any organic smell — pet, food, body — an enzyme cleaner digests what detergent masks. Full dwell time per the label. The [vomit-and-smells playbook](/blog/home-cleaning/how-to-get-vomit-stains-and-smells-out-of-a-couch/) covers the stubborn-odor escalation path.

**5. Dry completely, then deodorize.** Fans and sunlight until genuinely dry through the cushion. Finish with a generous baking-soda layer, a few hours' sit, and a final vacuum.

Budget a weekend: cleaning one day, drying the next. A used couch rushed back into service while damp is a mildew story waiting to start.

## When a Used Couch Isn't Worth the Work

Skip the project if the inspection finds pest evidence, mold, or soaked-in odor you can smell at arm's length — those are structural, not superficial. And if you've acquired one that turns out to be past saving, don't inherit the previous owner's disposal problem on the curb: [removal is priced upfront](/couch-removal/), and the couch you *actually* want can take its place this week.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How do you disinfect a secondhand couch?

Heat is the honest answer: hot-wash removable covers at 130°F+ and steam clean the body if the care tag allows water. Sprays sanitize surfaces; heat reaches into fabric.

### Can you get bed bugs from a used couch?

Yes — used upholstered furniture is one of the most common ways infestations spread. Inspect seams and crevices before purchase, and walk away from any evidence. No post-purchase cleaning method is reliable against them.

### How much does it cost to clean a used couch yourself?

Typically the price of a steam-cleaner rental plus supplies — enzyme cleaner, baking soda — which usually totals well under what a professional cleaning costs. The bigger investment is the weekend.

### What if the used couch smells after cleaning?

Odor that survives a full enzyme treatment is in the foam, and foam doesn't give it back. At that point you're choosing between living with it and [replacing it](/pricing/) — our guide on [why cleaned couches still smell](/blog/home-cleaning/how-to-get-pet-odors-out-of-sofas-and-rugs/) explains the chemistry.
